content:
If two elements differ by \(1\), the difference divides their sum. If they differ by \(2\), they have the same parity, so their sum is even and again the difference divides the sum. Thus no three consecutive integers can all contain more than one element of \(S\).

Partition
\[
\{1,2,3\},\{4,5,6\},\ldots,\{2011,2012,2013\},\{2014,2015\}.
\]
There are \(671\) triples and one pair, so
\[
|S|\le 671+1=672.
\]

Now take
\[
S=\{1,4,7,\ldots,2014\},
\]
which has \(672\) elements. For any two elements \(a,b\in S\), their difference is divisible by \(3\), while
\[
a+b\equiv 1+1\equiv 2 \pmod 3,
\]
so the difference cannot divide the sum. Hence this set is valid.

Therefore the maximum possible size is
\[
\boxed{672}.
\]
